               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 And when he had fasted forty days, and for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty nights, he was afterwards an hungred.<ns0:note place="bottom">He was in the Wilderness, a place of Solitude, and so fitter for Satans purpose, and he was an <ns0:hi>Hungred,</ns0:hi> which was ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther advantage Satan had. But he was not an Hungred, till <ns0:hi>he had fasted forty Days, and forty Nights.</ns0:hi> Here was the Divine Power miraculously seen, in upholding the Hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mane Nature of Christ, without any thing to eat: This was a Miracle, the like did <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> before the Law, <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> under the Law. Christ doth the same in the beginning of the <ns0:hi>Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel,</ns0:hi> nor did he fast as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were wont, of whom we sometimes read, that they kept Fasts several days, they only fasted in the Day-time, but ate their Food at Night, or some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times only <ns0:hi>forbare pleasant Bread,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> did, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 10.2.3. for three full Weeks. But Christ fasted from all Food, and that not only <ns0:hi>forty Days,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>forty Nights</ns0:hi> also, from whence may easily be gathered, how idly if not impiously, the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> found their fasting <ns0:hi>forty Days,</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Lent.</ns0:hi> Here all Christs Acts (most certainly his Miraculous works) are not recorded for our Imitation: Some of them are only for our <ns0:hi>Adoration,</ns0:hi> all his miraculous Acts are so. There can be no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing more sottish, then for us to think, that because Christ (supported by the Divine Nature) fasted forty Days, there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore we are obliged to do it, and because we cannot fast forty Days, and forty Nights, without eating something, there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore we may eat Fish, tho no Flesh (when all know that to some Pallats, there is no more delicate Food, then Fish) or we are obliged to fast in the Day-time, tho not at Night. And because Christ once in his Life-time fasted forty Days, and forty Nights, therefore we must do so every year, or that the Church hath any Power to injoyn any such thing. If <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> think, Christs fast of forty Days, and forty Nights, obligeth them to imitation, let them keep them as he did (with such a Fasting I mean) and try whether they be able to do it, or whether four Days or Nights, instead of forty will not Convince them of their Folly. Christ fasted forty Days, and forty Nights, and thereby shewed he was <ns0:hi>God-Man,</ns0:hi> the Divine Nature supported the Humane, afterward he was <ns0:hi>Hungry,</ns0:hi> to shew that he was truly <ns0:hi>Man touched with the feeling of our Infirmities, in all Points Tempted</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>we are, yet without sin, Heb</ns0:hi> 4.15.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And when the Tempter came unto him he said, If thou be the Son of God command that these stones be made Bread.<ns0:note place="bottom">And when the Tempter. [<ns0:hi>Satan,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> as he is called <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi>] <ns0:hi>came unto him,</ns0:hi> Probably in some visible shape. He forming an audible Voice of the Air said, <ns0:hi>If thou be the Son of God,</ns0:hi> not that he doubted it, which shewed his hor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rible Impudence. <ns0:hi>Command that these stones,</ns0:hi> this stone saith <ns0:hi>Luk. ch.</ns0:hi> 4.3. <ns0:hi>be made Bread.</ns0:hi> The Temptation plainly was <ns0:hi>to the use of means which God did not allow him, to relieve him in his Distress of Hunger, to</ns0:hi> distrust the <ns0:hi>Providence of God,</ns0:hi> in supporting of him. A Temptation common to those who are the Members of Christ, and enough to instruct us, that we ought to look upon all Thoughts, and Motions, to the use of means not allowed by God, in order to a Lawful end, as are <ns0:hi>Temptations vel a Carne,</ns0:hi> vel <ns0:hi>Hoste,</ns0:hi> either from our own Flesh, for <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.14. <ns0:hi>every man is Tempted, when he is drawn away by his own Lust,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>enticed</ns0:hi>; or from our <ns0:hi>Grand Adversary</ns0:hi> the Devil. It is not much material for us to know from which, they being both what we ought to resist, tho those from Satan are usually more violent, and impetuous.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 But he answered, and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">So also <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.4. There is no better answering the <ns0:hi>Tempter,</ns0:hi> then by opposing the Precepts of Holy-writ, to his <ns0:hi>Motions to sin.</ns0:hi> The word is called, The <ns0:hi>Sword of the Spirit, Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.17. The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> therefore denying People the use of the word, disarm them as to the <ns0:hi>Spiritual Combate.</ns0:hi> It is written <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 8.3. Tho man ordinarily liveth by common Bread, such Food as men usually eat, yet God's Power is not restrained, he can uphold the Life of Man when that is wanting, as he supported the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Manna</ns0:hi> (to which that Text re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lates) nor is God obliged to create any extraordinary mean, for his <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> which is seen in creating such means, can pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duce the same Effect without such a mean if it pleaseth him: His Power must be seen in creating the mean, and in upholding the Proper Power and Faculty of the mean, in order to its end, why cannot he by the same Power produce the Effect without any such mean?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 Then the Devil taketh him up into the ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly City, and setteth him on a Pinacle of the Temple.<ns0:note place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Holy City,</ns0:hi> is meant <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> once an Holy City, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.24. now tho a most impure, and filthy City, upon many Accounts, yet upon other Accounts still an <ns0:hi>Holy City</ns0:hi>; being the only City in the World, which had then in it the true Worship of the true God, and in which God, doubtless, who in <ns0:hi>Ahab's</ns0:hi> time had seven thousand in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> had many Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly People, how the Devil took Christ into the <ns0:hi>Holy City,</ns0:hi> is variously argued, and judged, the word used in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> are such as would incline us to think, he was not carried by Force, but followed the <ns0:hi>Tempter</ns0:hi> willingly, and set upon a place on the <ns0:hi>top of the Temple,</ns0:hi> higher then the other parts of it: The end of his being set there, the next Verse tells us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And saith unto him, if thou be the Son of God, cast thy self down, for it is written, He shall give his Angels charge concerning thee, and in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.<ns0:note place="bottom">Before the Devil had Tempted our Lord, to diffidence or distrust in Gods Providence, and the use of means not allowed by God to supply himself: Here he Tempts him <ns0:hi>to an un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />warrantable Presumption, and Confidence of, and concern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Divine Protection.</ns0:hi> In the former Temptation, the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> used no Scripture, but having been repelled in that Assault, <ns0:hi>by the Sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.17. He here takes up the same Weapon: The thing to which the <ns0:hi>Tempter</ns0:hi> solliciteth our Saviour, was the <ns0:hi>throwing himself down from a Precip<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ce,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Temptation</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Effect,</ns0:hi> to destroy himself (which is one of those Fiery Darts, which he commonly throweth at the People of God, in their hours of <ns0:hi>Melancholly,</ns0:hi> or under great Pressures of affliction) but the usual Argument, which he useth to them, is <ns0:hi>Deliverance from their Terrors,</ns0:hi> the preventing of want<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or avoiding Shame. The Argument he useth to our Lord is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ite of another Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, the <ns0:hi>special Protection of God,</ns0:hi> promised to Gods People, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 91. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11, 12. herein he transformeth himself into an <ns0:hi>Angel of Light,</ns0:hi> according to 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.14. and lets us know that Truth may be abused to the Patronage of lyes, and that there is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o hook more dangerous to the Members of Christ, than that which is baited with Scripture mis-in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreted, and mis-applyed: Which Holy-writ always is, when it is so interpreted, or so applyed as to be made an Argu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment to sin. This Portion of Holy-writ is both. 1. <ns0:hi>Falsely cued,</ns0:hi> and, 2 As <ns0:hi>ill app<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>yed.</ns0:hi> In the Quotation the Te<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>pter leaves out those words [<ns0:hi>in all thy ways</ns0:hi>] This was none of our Saviours <ns0:hi>ways,</ns0:hi> he had <ns0:hi>no call, no Warrant</ns0:hi> from God to decline the <ns0:hi>Stairs</ns0:hi> by which he might have gone down, and to throw himself down. God had never promised, nor ever gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven any the Protection of <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> in sinful, and forbidden ways<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 2 He <ns0:hi>mis-applyeth this Text,</ns0:hi> using it not to instruct, but to deceive, dividing betwixt, Mans Duty, and Gods Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vidence, making this word a Promise to be fulfilled, upon Christs neglect of his Duty, extending the Promise of <ns0:hi>special Providence,</ns0:hi> as to Dangers, into which men voluntarily throw themselves. Putting God upon working Miracles to declare Christ to be his Son, where there was no need, and of which there was no use, mocking our Saviours true use o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Scripture, with Scripture abused, and many other ways, but he had to do with one not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>gnorant of his devices.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:223" />7 Jesus saith unto him: It is written again, thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.<ns0:note place="bottom">This is written, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.16. To make an <ns0:hi>undue,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />warrantable Tryal of God, is to tempt God,</ns0:hi> whether the <ns0:hi>Trya<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> respecteth his <ns0:hi>Power,</ns0:hi> or his <ns0:hi>Goodness,</ns0:hi> thus the word used, <ns0:hi>Num</ns0:hi> 14.22. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 78.18. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.12. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 16.1. By this Answer Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> lets the Devil know that he abused Scripture in his Quotati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of it, such a casting of himself down, when he had a plain way to go down by the <ns0:hi>Stairs,</ns0:hi> would not have been an Act of <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Presumption,</ns0:hi> not a <ns0:hi>trusting</ns0:hi> God upon his word, but a <ns0:hi>Tempting</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi> expressly contrary to his Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mand. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.16.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Again, the Devil taketh him up into an ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceeding high Mountain, and sheweth him all the Kingdoms of the world, and the Glory of them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 And saith unto him, all these things will<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.<ns0:note place="bottom">This is the third <ns0:hi>Temptation,</ns0:hi> by which the <ns0:hi>Tempter</ns0:hi> solli<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>citeth our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> to sin, and of all other the most Impudent. For what can be more Impudent, than for the Creature to expect an Homage to him from him who was his Creator What Mountain this was, and how our Saviour was taken up into it, are things not revealed, and of very little concern for us to know. The Text tells us it was <ns0:hi>exceeding high,</ns0:hi> yet not high enough, from whence one Kingdom could be seen, in the extent of it. It is therefore most probable that Dr. <ns0:hi>Light<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />foot</ns0:hi> judgeth most truly. <ns0:hi>That the Devil, being the Prince of the Power of the Air, formed an Airy Horizon before the Eyes of Christ, carrying such Pompous, and Glorious ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pearance of Kingdoms, States,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Royalties in the Face of it, as if he had seen those very Kingdoms, and States indeed</ns0:hi> Such things the Devil can do, and doth do, by condensating the Air first, then shaping, and Figuring, and lastly so Colouring it, that it may represent what he intendeth. All these things he promised to give our Saviour, if he would fall down and Worship him. The same eminent Person well observes, that what <ns0:hi>Luke calls Worshipping before the Devil, Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew</ns0:hi> calls <ns0:hi>Worshipping the Devil,</ns0:hi> and concludes solidly. <ns0:hi>That if to Worship before the Devil, be to Worship the Devil Worshipping before an Image</ns0:hi> (as the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> do) <ns0:hi>must be Worshipping the Image.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Devil,</ns0:hi> here arrogates to him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, what was Gods alone to give, and such ordinarily are the <ns0:hi>Devils</ns0:hi> Promises, of things, as to which he hath no Pow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er to fulfil what he Promiseth.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence Satan, for it is written, <ns0:note place="margin">1 Sam. 7.3.</ns0:note> Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.<ns0:note place="bottom">As this was of all the three the most impudent Tempta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, so our Lord receiveth it with the highest Detestation, saying<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Get thee hence Satan</ns0:hi>! By which words, he doth not only shew his Detestation of this <ns0:hi>Temptation,</ns0:hi> but also chides him off from any further Tempting him. The Sense is, <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tan</ns0:hi> I know better things. <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That a Religious Adoration<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> is not to be given unto any, but unto God alone, thou art a <ns0:hi>Creature,</ns0:hi> no Worship is due unto thee: To <ns0:hi>Worship be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore thee</ns0:hi> (so <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> Phraseth it, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.7.) is to <ns0:hi>Worship thee.</ns0:hi> This is expressly contrary to the Command of God. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13. and 10.20. It is also observable, that our Saviour opposeth this to the Devils words, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. If thou falling down will Worship me, and that Christ answers, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> which shews the Idleness of the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> distinction of <ns0:hi>Doulia,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Latre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>a</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the first of which they say may be given to the Creature: The second only unto God, by which they justi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e their <ns0:hi>Veneration</ns0:hi> of Images? The using a <ns0:hi>posture of Adorati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on,</ns0:hi> before the <ns0:hi>Creature</ns0:hi> in an Act of Worship; Christ here in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreteth a <ns0:hi>Worshipping</ns0:hi> the Creature, if the Creature e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ther exacts it of us<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or we purposely set it before us<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or chuse it as an object exciting, or moving us to such an Act of Adoration, which the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> do not, that all <ns0:hi>Prostration</ns0:hi> before the Creature is an Act of <ns0:hi>Divine Adoration,</ns0:hi> there is a <ns0:hi>Civil,</ns0:hi> as well as a <ns0:hi>Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vine Worship,</ns0:hi> and in Divine Worship, the Position of the Creature before us, may be meerly for Conveniency, or Ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cidental: But all <ns0:hi>Prostration</ns0:hi> in an Act of <ns0:hi>Divine Worship,</ns0:hi> is a <ns0:hi>Posture of Adoration,</ns0:hi> and where a Creature is chosen, and set before us in that Act or Posture, to excite or move us, it partaketh of the Homage. There is some little difference betwixt the words, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 6.13. and 10.20. and those of St. <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> but that is said to be <ns0:hi>written,</ns0:hi> which is written as to the Substance and Sense, tho not in those Terms. <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Thou shalt fear,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> quotes it, it is, <ns0:hi>Thou shalt Worship.</ns0:hi> The Term <ns0:hi>Fear</ns0:hi> applied unto God, signifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth any Act of Religion, whether <ns0:hi>External</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Internal,</ns0:hi> and tho the last words in <ns0:hi>Deuteron.</ns0:hi> [<ns0:hi>thou sha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>t swear by his Name</ns0:hi>] be not mentioned in <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> yet enough are quoted for our Saviours purpose. <ns0:hi>Falling</ns0:hi> down and <ns0:hi>Worshipping,</ns0:hi> belongeth only to God (saith our Saviour) not to thee, let me therefore hear of thee no more.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Then the Devil leaveth him, and behold Angels came and ministred unto him.<ns0:note place="bottom">Resist the <ns0:hi>Devil</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Iames ch.</ns0:hi> 4.7. and <ns0:hi>he shall flee from you,</ns0:hi> thus he did from the Head, thus he shall do from the Members, but as he did not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ee from Christ, till Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded away, so neither till Commanded o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> by God, doth he leave the People of God, but upon our <ns0:hi>resistance,</ns0:hi> God will Command him off, that we may not be Tempted above our strength. The <ns0:hi>Evil Angels</ns0:hi> leaving him, the Good Angels came and ministred unto him, whether by bringing him Food, or bringing him off the Mount, or otherwise Executing his Commands, is not expressed, and it is too much Curiosity to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quire. God by this teacheth us, that our Lives are to have their Vici<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>situdes of Temptations, and Consolations, and that our Temptations shall have an happy <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and that when ordinary means fail, we may expect extraordinary Influences, and Assistances. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, he <ns0:hi>departed from him for a Sea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son</ns0:hi>: To let us know, that tho here was an end of his more eminent Temptations, yet he was not afterward without Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tans Assaults.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 1.14. Luk. 3.20.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 4.14.31. Joh. 4.43.</ns0:note> Now when Jesus had heard that John was <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>delivered up.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> cast into Prison, he departed into Galilee.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was some time after this cast into Prison, for his free reproving <ns0:hi>Herod Antipas,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Tetrarch of Galilee,</ns0:hi> for taking <ns0:hi>Herodias</ns0:hi> his Brother <ns0:hi>Phillips</ns0:hi> Wife, and other Evils, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.3.4. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 6.17. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 3.19, 20. <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> heard of this accident, and <ns0:hi>departed into Galilee.</ns0:hi> There were many things happened betwixt Christ's <ns0:hi>Temptations,</ns0:hi> and this his Motion into <ns0:hi>Gali<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ee,</ns0:hi> which are omitted by all the Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists except <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>

               </ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="16">16 The People which sate in darkness, saw great light, and to them which sate in the Regi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, and shadow of death, light is sprang up.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Text in <ns0:hi>Isaiah,</ns0:hi> 9.1.2. where the words are, <ns0:hi>Ne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vertheless the Dimness shall not be such as was in her Vexa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, when at the first he lightly afflicted the Land of Ze<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bulon, and the Land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the Sea beyond Iordan, in Galilee of the Nations. The People that walked in Dark<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, have seen a great Light, they that dwell in the Land of the shadow of Death, upon them hath a Light shined.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> make a great many Objections against the Appli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of this Text unto Christ (as indeed they do against the Application of all Texts cited out of the Old Testament by the Evangelists) Christians believing that the Evangelists be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Holy Men, who wrote not from a private Spirit, private Interpretations, have not any reason to regard what their In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terest leadeth them to Object: But even Christian Interpreters are divided in their Sentiments whether these words are said to be fulfilled, in this Motion of Christ unto <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> in a <ns0:hi>Lite<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Typical,</ns0:hi> or a more <ns0:hi>improper</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Analogical Sense,</ns0:hi> nor is it any great matter with which of them we agree, for my own part, I see no reason, why, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2. should not be Litterally understood of, and applyed unto Christ. There is nothing more ordinary in the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> than after a threat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning of Judgment, and Captivity unto the People to Comfort such as feared God amongst them with Promises of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and the spiritual Salvation which was to be brought in; The Land of <ns0:hi>Zebulon,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Naphtali,</ns0:hi> suffered much by <ns0:hi>Ben<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hadad,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 15.20. and more by <ns0:hi>Tiglath-Pilezer,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 15.29. before the General Captivity of the ten Tribes, 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 17.6. The Lord by the Prophet, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8. had been threatning this <ns0:hi>general Captivity,</ns0:hi> possibly the Prophet might say, the Affliction of those parts, should not be so great as the second mentioned, 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 15.20. because by the story it seems they were generally carried into Captivity, before the more <ns0:hi>gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Destruction</ns0:hi> of the other Tribes there, saith he. This <ns0:hi>Dark<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness</ns0:hi> shall be abundantly hereafter compensated, by the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and Preaching amongst this People; who living at a great distance from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi>; never had such a Light as some other parts of <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> and first drank of the Cup of Gods wrath in their Captivity. It was called <ns0:hi>Galilee of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> because it was near to the Men of <ns0:hi>Tyre,</ns0:hi> who were <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and had doubtless, in it a greater mixture o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>d.<ns0:note place="bottom">From the time of Christs Baptism, or from the time that he heard that <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was committed to Prison, he, who before had Preached and taught privately, and more rarely, began to Preach more ordinarily, and publikely, and the sum of his Doctrine, was the same with that of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptist,</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firming his Doctrine, <ns0:hi>Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.</ns0:hi> See the Sense of those words, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 1.14.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="18">18 And Jesus walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 1.16. Joh. 1.42.</ns0:note> called Peter, and An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />drew his Brother, casting a net into the Sea for they were Fishers<ns0:note place="bottom">Whether by the Sea, he here meant the Lake of <ns0:hi>Gennesaret</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Ocean,</ns0:hi> is not worth the arguing, for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> called all great Collections of waters the <ns0:hi>Seas</ns0:hi> according to <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1.10. <ns0:hi>he saw two Brethren Simon called Peter, and Andrew his Bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther,</ns0:hi> whether natural Brethren, or called so because of their joynt Imployment, <ns0:hi>casting a Net into the Sea,</ns0:hi> either, for the catching of Fish, or for the washing of their Nets, see <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 5.2. <ns0:hi>for they were Fisher-men,</ns0:hi> Sea-men (as the word seems to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ignifie) used to fish in the Sea; <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> had a Ship of his own, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 5.3. The Evangelists differing Relation of the call of <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Andrew,</ns0:hi> hath made a great deal of work for In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters. The greatest difference seemeth to be betwixt <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> in this Text, and <ns0:hi>Iohn, ch.</ns0:hi> 1.35, 36, 37, 38. But certainly <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> speaketh of one <ns0:hi>Call</ns0:hi> in those Verses: The o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> of another. According to <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> they were <ns0:hi>called</ns0:hi> to the knowledge of, and first Acquaintance with Christ, this was while <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was in the publike Exercise of his Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stry, for they were his Disciples, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.35, 36. and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 39. they are said at that time, <ns0:hi>to have abode with him that day</ns0:hi>: Probably they again returned to their old Imployment, and when <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was imprisoned, Christ walking by the Sea, saw them, and then called them to the Apostle-ship. There are other differences in their Call observed, betwixt <ns0:hi>Matthew, Mark</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> but such as may be easily answered, by those who observe that there is nothing more ordinary, than for the <ns0:hi>Evangelists</ns0:hi> in reporting the same History, one of them to supply more largely what the other had recorded more sum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />marily.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you Fishers of men.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here was their Call to the Office of <ns0:hi>Apostles.</ns0:hi> It is obser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vable that Gods Calls of men to places of Dignity, and Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nour, and his appearances of Favour to them, have ordinarily been when they have been busied in the honest Imployments of their Callings. <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> was seeking his Fathers Asses, <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> keeping his Fathers Sheep, when the Lord called them to the Kingdom: The <ns0:hi>Shepheards</ns0:hi> were feeding their Flocks, when they had the Revel<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tion of Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, he calleth four <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> from their Fishery. <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> from amongst the Herdmen of <ns0:hi>Tekoah, Matthew</ns0:hi> from the rece<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t of Custom, <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> when keeping <ns0:hi>Iethroe</ns0:hi>'s Flock, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 3.2. <ns0:hi>Gideon</ns0:hi> from the Thresh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing floor, <ns0:hi>Iud.</ns0:hi> 6.11. God never incourageth Idleness, but despiseth not Persons in meanest Imployments. <ns0:hi>Follow me,</ns0:hi> that is, to return no more to your Imployment. [<ns0:hi>I will make you Fishers of Men</ns0:hi>] Here is the work of Mini<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ers set out, to gain Souls to God, they are not to <ns0:hi>Fish</ns0:hi> meerly for a Live<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lihood, much less for Honour and applause to themselves, but to win Souls to God, and are to bait their Hooks, and or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r Nets to this end<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which they will never serve, if ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />their by general Discourses, they make the Maskes so wide, that all will dart through them, or if by their Wit, and Lear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning, they make their Discourses so fine, and curious, that few or none of their Hearers can understand them. Nor will all our Art make us Fishers of Men: <ns0:hi>I will make you</ns0:hi> (saith Christ) <ns0:hi>Paul may plant,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Appollos</ns0:hi> may water, God <ns0:hi>must give the increase</ns0:hi>: But yet we must order our Nets rationally, and probably in order to our end, and without that, can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not expect Gods blessings. Nor were the Apostles presently to enter upon the work of the Ministry, but first to <ns0:hi>follow him.</ns0:hi> And indeed such should all Gospel Ministers be, in the choice of <ns0:hi>Matthias, Peter</ns0:hi> limited the People in their Electi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, to <ns0:hi>those that had accompanied with them all the time, the Lord Iesus went in and out amongst them, Acts</ns0:hi> 1.21. other Ministers commonly prove <ns0:hi>Fishers</ns0:hi> for something else not for the Souls of men.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And they straightway left <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> Nets, and followed him.<ns0:note place="bottom">When Christ calls, Men shall obey, when he calls, he draweth. It is not of indespensable necessity, that men who exercise the Ministry should have nothing else to do, <ns0:hi>Pauls hands ministred to his Necessities.</ns0:hi> But nothing but a providing for our selves, and Housholds, can excuse Ministers, in intangling themselves with the things of this Life. <ns0:hi>Churches</ns0:hi> that are able ought better to provide for their Ministers, and Ministers so provided for, sin if they do not <ns0:hi>wholly give up themselves to their work,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.15.</ns0:note>

So as they immediately left their Ship, and their <ns0:hi>Father,</ns0:hi> else<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />where the D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sc<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ples say, <ns0:hi>Master we have left all</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>followed thee,</ns0:hi> probably their Imployment with their Ship was their <ns0:hi>All.</ns0:hi> They left <ns0:hi>their Father</ns0:hi> also, but it was upon <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Call,</ns0:hi> in which Case it is every Mans Duty (<ns0:hi>and followed him</ns0:hi>) to learn of him before they went out to <ns0:hi>Preach him,</ns0:hi> and to be Witnesses of his <ns0:hi>Miracles, &c.</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="23">23 And Jesus went about all Galilee teaching in their Synagogues, and Preaching the Gospel of the Kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the People.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iesus Christ</ns0:hi> having now called <ns0:hi>four Disciples,</ns0:hi> did not judge it sufficient to send them about, but himself went about all the places of that dark Country of <ns0:hi>Galilee [teaching in their Synagogues]</ns0:hi> the word signifieth both the <ns0:hi>Congregation</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vened, and the <ns0:hi>Place.</ns0:hi> Here it signifieth both: <ns0:hi>Synagogues</ns0:hi> were of old time, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.21. How ancient we know not. Some think that they were no older than the return out of the Captivity of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi>: But I am posed then in determi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning, where the Body of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> ordinarily worshipped God on the <ns0:hi>Sabbath-days,</ns0:hi> for it is certain they did not all go up to the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> In the <ns0:hi>Old Testament</ns0:hi> we read of them only, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 74.8. as at that time <ns0:hi>burnt up</ns0:hi>: As to the order of them we only read. That they had some <ns0:hi>Rulers, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.15. who directed those who were to speak <ns0:hi>words of Exhortation.</ns0:hi> The Scriptures were read in them, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.21. the <ns0:hi>Law</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Prophets, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.15. They <ns0:hi>prayed</ns0:hi> in them, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 6.5. they expounded Scripture in them, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.16, 17, 18, 19. Christ [<ns0:hi>Preached in the Synagogues</ns0:hi>] not only there, we shall find him Preaching on the <ns0:hi>Mount</ns0:hi> in the next <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> and in <ns0:hi>private Houses,</ns0:hi> but he did not <ns0:hi>decline</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Sy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nagogues</ns0:hi>: Either, as to <ns0:hi>Preaching, or Hearing,</ns0:hi> not wholly separating from a <ns0:hi>Church</ns0:hi> corrupt enough through <ns0:hi>Tradi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions,</ns0:hi> but not <ns0:hi>Idolatrous,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>what</ns0:hi> did he Preach? <ns0:hi>The Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel of the Kingdom,</ns0:hi> the glad Tidings for lost Sinners, that was come into the World, by the Revelation of him, who was the true <ns0:hi>Messias,</ns0:hi> and the true and only way, by which Men might come to the Kingdomof God, and be eternally saved: This is what all his Ministers should publish, not their own Conceits, or Dictates of Men, or things impertinent to the Salvation of Souls, but the <ns0:hi>Gospel of the Kingdom, and heal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing all manner of Sicknesses, and all manner of Diseases a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongst the People.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is all Diseases, and Sicknesses, yet surely some dyed in <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> in that time.                      </ns0:gap>s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> is said to be bounded on the North by <ns0:hi>Cilicia</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> on the <ns0:hi>South,</ns0:hi> on the <ns0:hi>West</ns0:hi> with the <ns0:hi>Sea,</ns0:hi> and on the <ns0:hi>East,</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Euphrates,</ns0:hi> and to comprehend within it all <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dea, Bethany, Galilee, Decapol<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s, Samaria, Idumea, Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lestina, Syrophoenicia, Syria</ns0:hi>; of <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioch.</ns0:hi> Christs fame spread very far doubtless, because of the good he did, and the Miracles he wrought <ns0:hi>[and they brought out to him, all such People, that were taken with divers Diseases] All</ns0:hi> here again can signifie no more than <ns0:hi>very many</ns0:hi> that were indisposed, and ill affected as to their bodily Health, those that were Sick of, or detained in their Beds, or Houses by <ns0:hi>divers Diseases:</ns0:hi> Tho Christ shewed his <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> in curing some Diseases, which Physicians judge incura<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rable, yet he shewed his kindness also in relieving others, not so fatally Sick [and <ns0:hi>Torments</ns0:hi>] such as were troubled with great Pains, as if they were upon <ns0:hi>Racks,</ns0:hi> or in the hands of Tormentors, that set themselves to Torture them [<ns0:hi>and those which were possessed with Devils</ns0:hi>] Of these sorts of Persons<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> we shall read often in the Gospel: This is the fir<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t time, we meet with the term. It is observed that in the Old Te<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tament we read little of any such Persons (we read only of <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>'s be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing vexed with an <ns0:hi>evil Spirit</ns0:hi>) we read much of them in the New Testament, and in <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical History,</ns0:hi> for some years after Christ, they called them <ns0:hi>Energumeni.</ns0:hi> Some think God in those first times of the Gospel permitted, the Devil to this degree, that the <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> of our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> might be the more seen casting them out, and in giving Authority to his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples to cast them out, which was a great Demon<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tration of his Divinity: Others think, that God did it for a Demonstra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of the Error of the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> who held <ns0:hi>there was no Spirits.</ns0:hi> The Gospel seemeth to hint two sorts of these Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons. Some upon whom the Devil had Power, no further than to <ns0:hi>Wrack</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Torture</ns0:hi> them. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 5.3, 4, 5. <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 9.39. others, in whom he dwelled Bodily, and Divined, and Prophecied in them, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 16.16. [<ns0:hi>and those which were Lu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />natick</ns0:hi>) affected with such Diseases, as use to increase, in some times of the Moon, or at such times to seize Persons of this Nature, we know divers more particularly, the <ns0:hi>Falling Sick<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Dropsie</ns0:hi> [<ns0:hi>and those which had the Palsie</ns0:hi>] a Disease caused by the Resolution of the <ns0:hi>Nerves.</ns0:hi> Those Diseases are mentioned, which Men account hardest to be cured, if capable of Cure by Men, Christ to shew his Divine Power <ns0:hi>healed them.</ns0:hi> Christ did not only cure these Bodily Di<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>empers, but he also Preached the Gospel of the Kingdom to heal their Soul Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stempers: We read of many came to him for Bodily Cure, but of none that said to him: <ns0:hi>What shall we do to be saved?</ns0:hi> How sensible are Men and Women of their Bodily Pains, and Diseases more than of their Souls wants?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> Decapolis, and <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> Jerusalem, and <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> Judea, and <ns0:hi>from</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yond Jordan.<ns0:note place="bottom">They followed for the <ns0:hi>Loaves,</ns0:hi> for the benefit of the Bodi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly Cures, or out of Curiosity, tho some (probably) follow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed him out of Love, and to learn of him, <ns0:hi>Decapolis</ns0:hi> hath its name from ten Cities, comprehended in it. Here was a mix<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture both of <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> following Christ, who came to be a Saviour of them both, and to pull down the <ns0:hi>Partition<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wall</ns0:hi> betwixt both, to make them both one <ns0:hi>Gospel-Church, Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.14.</ns0:note>
